conclusion.justification: The report explicitly states that the claim is false and contradicts a substantial body of peer-reviewed research showing flu vaccines are associated with reduced, rather than increased, risk of Alzheimer's disease.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
Your skepticism is well-supported: the claim that flu vaccination causes Alzheimer's disease is false, and the scientific evidence points the opposite direction.

**Origin of the myth:** The claim traces largely to a widely circulated, unsubstantiated assertion attributed to immunologist Hugh Fudenberg, alleging that five consecutive flu shots increased Alzheimer's risk tenfold, supposedly due to mercury/aluminum in vaccines. This claim has never been published in a peer-reviewed study and is treated as a fringe/anti-vaccine talking point (https://homeopathicassociates.com/flu-shots-cause-alzheimers/, https://www.lewrockwell.com/2008/10/donald-w-miller-jr-md/dont-get-a-flu-shot-2/).

**What actual research shows:** The Alzheimer's Drug Discovery Foundation explicitly labels this a myth, stating "there is no peer-reviewed scientific evidence supporting this claim," and instead cites evidence of a decreased dementia risk associated with flu vaccination (https://www.alzdiscovery.org/cognitive-vitality/blog/is-there-a-link-between-alzheimers-disease-and-the-flu-shot).

Multiple peer-reviewed cohort studies reinforce this. Research published via PMC found reduced Alzheimer's risk after influenza vaccination in older adults (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9484126/). A 2026 study in *Neurology* found high-dose flu vaccines reduced incident Alzheimer's dementia risk compared to standard-dose vaccines, especially in women (https://www.neurology.org/doi/10.1212/WNL.0000000000214782). A broader analysis in *Age and Ageing* similarly found that adult vaccinations—including influenza—correlate with lower dementia risk (https://academic.oup.com/ageing/article/54/11/afaf331/8339764).

**Conclusion:** The claim is false. It originated from an unverified, non-peer-reviewed source and contradicts a substantial and growing body of peer-reviewed research showing influenza vaccination is associated with *reduced*, not increased, Alzheimer's risk.
